\section[verschwenden]{verschwenden — to waste}

\label{lesson:GE-C390-verschwenden}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the German for the expense, then the German for the income.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: verschwenden}
\textbf{verschwenden} — \textquotedblleft{}to waste\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Er verschwendet viel Geld für Kleidung.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{He wastes a lot of money on clothes.}
\end{quote}

Inseparable: \emph{er verschwendet, er hat verschwendet}. \emph{Zeit verschwenden} — to waste time.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{verschwenden} is inherited from Middle High German \emph{verswenden} and Old High German \emph{firswenten} (EtymDB), \textquotedblleft{}to make vanish\textquotedblright{}, of the family of \emph{schwinden} \textquotedblleft{}to dwindle\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{verschwenden}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{verschwenden}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{verschwenden}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the German for the expense, then the German for the income, then say \emph{verschwenden} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does verschwenden mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To waste\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[die Verschwendung]{die Verschwendung — the waste}

\label{lesson:GE-C390-verschwendung}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the German for the income, then the German for to waste.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: die Verschwendung}
\textbf{die Verschwendung} — \textquotedblleft{}the waste\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
So viel Essen wegzuwerfen ist reine Verschwendung.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Throwing away so much food is a pure waste.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Was für eine Verschwendung!} — what a waste!

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{Verschwendung} is the noun of \emph{verschwenden}, from Old High German \emph{firswenten} \textquotedblleft{}to make vanish\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB), with \emph{-ung}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[preiswert]{preiswert — good value, inexpensive}

\label{lesson:GE-C390-preiswert}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the German for to waste, then the German for the waste.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: preiswert}
\textbf{preiswert} — \textquotedblleft{}good value, inexpensive\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Das kleine Hotel war sauber und preiswert.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{The small hotel was clean and good value.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Preiswert} is a compliment: worth its price. \emph{Billig} can sound cheap and poor.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{preiswert} joins \emph{Preis} \textquotedblleft{}price\textquotedblright{}, from Old French \emph{pris} and Latin \emph{pretium} \textquotedblleft{}price, value\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short), to \emph{wert} \textquotedblleft{}worth\textquotedblright{}, Proto-Germanic \emph{werþaz} (EtymDB): worth its price.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[das Vermögen]{das Vermögen — the fortune, the assets}

\label{lesson:GE-C390-vermoegen}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the German for the waste, then the German for good value.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: das Vermögen}
\textbf{das Vermögen} — \textquotedblleft{}the fortune, the assets\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Die Familie hat ein großes Vermögen.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{The family has a large fortune.}
\end{quote}

Plural: \emph{die Vermögen}. In formal German also ability: \emph{nach bestem Vermögen} — to the best of your ability.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{Vermögen} is the old verb \emph{vermögen} \textquotedblleft{}to be able\textquotedblright{} made into a noun, built on \emph{mögen}, from Proto-Germanic \emph{maganą} \textquotedblleft{}to be able\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB): what your means let you do.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[die Zahlung]{die Zahlung — the payment}

\label{lesson:GE-C390-zahlung}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the German for good value, then the German for the fortune.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: die Zahlung}
\textbf{die Zahlung} — \textquotedblleft{}the payment\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Die Zahlung ist bis zum Zehnten des Monats fällig.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Payment is due by the tenth of the month.}
\end{quote}

Plural: \emph{die Zahlungen}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{Zahlung} is the noun of \emph{zahlen} \textquotedblleft{}to pay\textquotedblright{}, from \emph{Zahl} \textquotedblleft{}number\textquotedblright{}, Old High German \emph{zala}, Proto-Germanic \emph{talō} (EtymDB), with \emph{-ung}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}
